chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Do not befriend the people of innovation, nor sit with them, so that you become in the eyes of the people like one of them.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A man is upon the religion of his close friend and his companion.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبِدَعِ: People of innovation (those who introduce religious deviations)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on befriending people of religious innovation?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against socializing with Ahl al-Bid'ah to preserve communal identity and prevent the dilution of religious authenticity through association. This practical guidance is rooted in the Prophetic maxim that one's faith mirrors their close companion, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding social purity and theological distinctiveness. The warning highlights the sociological dimension of faith, where external perception and internal conviction are mutually reinforced by consistent companionship.
